method: 20 synthetic geometries run through the REAL compute_signals/table_shape_score functions (031/table_shape_probe.py, imported not reimplemented). Ground truth is defined by construction and explicitly marked AMBIGUOUS_BY_DESIGN for 2 cases where the milestone brief's own instruction ('do not force a binary answer where semantics are genuinely uncertain') applies.

cases.name: obvious table
cases.reasoning: regular 4x4 grid, every cell populated, no occlusion
score_reasons: multiple children per row (grid, not a list)

cases.name: obvious picture
cases.reasoning: zero nested text children -- a genuine photo/graphic

cases.name: obvious paragraph
cases.reasoning: single text child, no internal structure

cases.name: table under stamp
cases.reasoning: regular grid with a contiguous missing patch -- occlusion, not a different structure; a human recognizes this as a partially occluded table
score_reasons: multiple children per row (grid, not a list)

cases.name: table under heavy occlusion
cases.reasoning: checkerboard-pattern occlusion leaves only 8/16 cells -- genuinely marginal: row/col band counts may still register, but children_per_row_band drops sharply. Tests whether the score degrades gracefully or falls off a cliff.
score_reasons: multiple children per row (grid, not a list)

cases.name: table with sparse cells
cases.reasoning: a real but very sparse table (mostly-empty cells) -- few children relative to declared shape; tests whether low child count alone suppresses recovery of a genuinely sparse table
score_reasons: multiple children per row (grid, not a list)

cases.name: table with merged cells
cases.reasoning: row 0 is one wide merged header cell (col-span), rows 1-3 are a normal 4-col grid -- children_per_row_band varies sharply by row, which the CURRENT rank-based reconstruction (031 controlled_intervention.py) is known to handle poorly (cols_horizontally_coherent failures, 73/79 in 031's real population)
score_reasons: multiple children per row (grid, not a list)

cases.name: aligned paragraph
cases.reasoning: justified prose wraps into short lines of similar width -- single column (col_bands=1), so table_shape_score's multi-column criterion should reject it, but a POORLY chosen column-band tolerance could conceivably misfire; ground truth is text by construction (only one 'column' of content exists)

cases.name: form
cases.reasoning: a label/value form is STRUCTURALLY indistinguishable from a genuine 2-column table using ONLY geometric evidence (regular 6x2 grid) -- this is exactly Phase 2's 'form' category, and this repository's evidence model (031 Phase 4-6, 032 role_evidence_schema.json) has NO signal that distinguishes 'table' from 'form' when both are regular grids. Reported as genuinely ambiguous, not resolved by fiat.
score_reasons: multiple children per row (grid, not a list)

cases.name: chart
cases.reasoning: axis labels + title + legend are scattered, LOW density, irregular spacing -- geometrically closer to the confirmed-negative population (table_shape_probe.json) than to the confirmed-table population; ground truth: chart, not table, by construction

cases.name: stamp with aligned text
cases.reasoning: circular/ring text around a seal graphic -- only 3 children, row_bands likely <2 given the ring layout -- should score low; ground truth picture

cases.name: photo containing text
cases.reasoning: a photograph with one embedded sign/label -- 1 child, should score 0 (below AMBIGUOUS threshold in Phase 2's own scheme)

cases.name: screenshot of a table
cases.reasoning: a screenshot of a REAL table, rendered as a picture element by the detector, but structurally IS a genuine table -- identical geometry to case 1. Ground truth 'table' is NOT evaluator-uncertain semantically (it really is a table), but WOULD be uncertain for a real detector deciding picture-vs-table from pixels alone -- the uncertainty here is about the DETECTOR's task, not this script's labeling.
score_reasons: multiple children per row (grid, not a list)

cases.name: decorative grid
cases.reasoning: a regular 4x4 grid of EMPTY boxes (decorative table-look border, no text content at all) -- geometrically identical to case 1 (obvious table), text-content-empty. This is the sharpest test of whether text CONTENT (not just geometry) should gate recovery -- 031's actual reconstruct_table() does not check text emptiness at all, so this case would score identically to a real table and produce an all-empty pseudo-table if fired on.
score_reasons: multiple children per row (grid, not a list)

cases.name: textbook banner
cases.reasoning: EXACT geometry of the real confirmed false positive (jiaocaineedrop_Chapter9.pdf_46 region 0, negative_controls.json) -- included here as a synthetic control reproducing a REAL confirmed case, not a hypothetical one
score_reasons: multiple children per row (grid, not a list)

cases.name: signature block
cases.reasoning: 3 short children, 3 row bands, 1 column -- low children_per_row_band (1.0), should score low despite multi-row

cases.name: multi-column paragraph
cases.reasoning: 2 newspaper-style columns of prose -- col_bands=2, row_bands could register as high as the line count (8), children_per_row_band=2.0 -- this is GENUINELY the hardest misleading case: it can satisfy every criterion in table_shape_score (multi-row, multi-column, multiple children per row, regular spacing, high count) while being pure prose. Ground truth text by construction; flagged as the single most concerning case in this control set -- see FINAL_REPORT.
score_reasons: multiple children per row (grid, not a list)

cases.name: dense bullet list
cases.reasoning: single column, many rows -- col_bands=1 should reject it via the multi-column criterion

cases.name: pseudo-table (coincidental alignment)
cases.reasoning: repeated 'Label: value' lines align into a perfect 2-column grid purely because every line uses the same template -- geometrically IDENTICAL to case 9 (form). This is exactly the milestone's own named alternative explanation ('nested text children happen to form approximately aligned blocks... that does NOT prove they are table cells', 031's Phase 13 instruction) -- reported as ambiguous, not resolved.
score_reasons: multiple children per row (grid, not a list)

cases.name: malformed table
cases.reasoning: a REAL table with inconsistent per-row cell counts (bad OCR fragmentation, not occlusion) -- structurally messy but genuinely a table; tests whether irregular-but-real tables score similarly to occluded-but-real tables (case 4/5) or get penalized differently
score_reasons: multiple children per row (grid, not a list)

finding: 6 of 18 decidable cases misfire against the current conservative threshold (score>=3). The most important is case 17 (multi-column paragraph): pure prose that satisfies every criterion in table_shape_score. Cases 9 and 19 (form / pseudo-table) are marked AMBIGUOUS_BY_DESIGN rather than forced to a binary verdict, because this repository's current evidence model genuinely cannot distinguish them from a real table using only geometry -- this is not a probe bug, it is a real limit of geometry-only evidence.
